message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Markdown Validation

on:
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  check-md-files:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683  # v4.2.2
      with:
        persist-credentials: false
    - name: Set up Go
      uses: actions/setup-go@0a12ed9d6a96ab950c8f026ed9f722fe0da7ef32  # v5.0.2
      with:
        go-version: stable
    - name: Cache Go modules
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: |
          ~/go/pkg/mod
          ~/.cache/go-build
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-go-mod-${{ hashFiles('Makefile') }}
        restore-keys: |
          ${{ runner.os }}-go-mod-
    - name: Check for broken links
      run: |
        make check",
  "rationale": "The workflow runs `make check` on every pull request, and `make check` installs the pinned `mdox` Go tool via `go install github.com/bwplotka/mdox@<commit>` each run, repeatedly downloading and building the same dependency. The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern (dependency_cache) supports caching dependency downloads to reduce CI time; its preconditions are met (repeated dependency fetching, cache keyed on the pinned Makefile/environment) and no contraindications apply (the module version is pinned to an immutable commit, and no equivalent cache exists). Adding an `actions/cache` step for the Go module and build caches preserves the full `make check` coverage and requires no new permissions, secrets, publishing/deployment operations, or external network access beyond the existing GitHub Actions cache service.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE"]
}
